225	// series refs. Compaction callers only request AllPostings, which is served from the
226	// precomputed ref list without re-reading the Head. Other IndexReader methods delegate to
227	// the caller-supplied filter, which encodes the compaction flow's notion of "matching series".
228	type headSelectedSeriesIndexReader struct {
229		*headIndexReader
230		selectedSeriesRefs seriesRefs
231	}
232	
233	type allSelectedSeriesPostings struct{ index.Postings }
234	
235	func (h *headSelectedSeriesIndexReader) Postings(ctx context.Context, name string, values ...string) (index.Postings, error) {
236		if len(h.selectedSeriesRefs.sortedByRef) == 0 {
237			return index.EmptyPostings(), nil
238		}
239	
240		selectedSeriesPostings := index.NewListPostings(h.selectedSeriesRefs.sortedByRef)
241		// This method is only expected to be called during compaction from the AllSortedPostings, with AllPostingsKey.
242		// The result of this method will be passed to SortedPostings().
243		// In order to avoid sorting head twice, but still return the correct results, we return a postings type with a marker here.
244		// This marker will be used by SortedPostings to swap the full postings by the ones sorted by labels.
245		// However, the results is still valid to be used as normal postings as well.
246		if k, v := index.AllPostingsKey(); name == k && len(values) == 1 && values[0] == v {
247			return allSelectedSeriesPostings{selectedSeriesPostings}, nil
248		}
249	
250		// This is not expected to be used, as headSelectedSeriesIndexReader is only expected to be used during compaction.
251		return index.Intersect(selectedSeriesPostings, h.head.postings.Postings(ctx, name, values...)), nil
252	}
253	
254	func (h *headSelectedSeriesIndexReader) PostingsForLabelMatching(ctx context.Context, name string, match func(string) bool) index.Postings {
255		// This is not expected to be used, as headSelectedSeriesIndexReader is only expected to be used during compaction.
256		return index.Intersect(
257			index.NewListPostings(h.selectedSeriesRefs.sortedByRef),
258			h.head.postings.PostingsForLabelMatching(ctx, name, match),
259		)
260	}
261	
262	func (h *headSelectedSeriesIndexReader) PostingsForAllLabelValues(ctx context.Context, name string) index.Postings {
263		// This is not expected to be used, as headSelectedSeriesIndexReader is only expected to be used during compaction.
264		return index.Intersect(
265			index.NewListPostings(h.selectedSeriesRefs.sortedByRef),
266			h.head.postings.PostingsForAllLabelValues(ctx, name),
267		)
268	}

units.headline: New benchmark helper builds a head with N single-chunk series
units.summary: New test-only helper that opens a DB with compactions disabled and appends samplesPerSeries in-order samples for each of totalSeries series, committing every 10k series. It only runs in benchmarks, so there is no production impact.
units.reason: Test-only helper in a _test.go file; cannot affect production behavior.

units.headline: Benchmark for CompactSelectedSeries across selection fractions
units.summary: New benchmark that rebuilds the DB on every iteration and times only CompactSelectedSeries for selected fractions from 100% down to 0.1%. It is test-only. The comment about evicted series being non-reusable matches the destructive behavior.
units.reason: New benchmark only; no production code path.

units.headline: New public API compacts and evicts caller-chosen head series
units.summary: Adds a public DB method that drops refs with OOO data, writes one block per chunk range for the remaining series through compactHeadViewLocked, and evicts them from the head behind an appendID watermark guard. It adds triggered/failed/duration metrics and blocks tagged with the selected-series hint. This creates new persisted blocks and deletes series from the head.

issues.title: Duplicate refs in input likely make block write fail
issues.failure_scenario: A caller passes []SeriesRef{r, r}. filterSeriesAndSortPostings does not deduplicate, so sortedByLabels contains the same series twice. The index writer probably rejects the repeated label set as out of order, so the whole compaction fails and no series are evicted.

issues.title: num_skipped_ooo also counts missing and duplicate refs
issues.failure_scenario: Refs that are no longer in the head are dropped by the filter's nil-series check and still counted as skipped OOO in the log, which misattributes the cause.

issues.title: Series not evicted when head MinTime >= MaxTime
issues.failure_scenario: Every head sample has the same timestamp, e.g. a single sample at t=100. A block is written, but truncateSeries returns early, so the series stays in the head. A repeated call writes another overlapping block with the same data.

units.reason: New public API that writes blocks and deletes head series; persistence and locking need review.
focus: Whether callers may pass duplicate or unsorted refs, and how the block writer handles duplicates
The cmtx lock held during the whole block write and eviction, and how it interacts with regular compactions
Isolation-disabled mode: the watermark guard is a no-op, so a concurrent append to a selected series can be lost
Eviction silently skipped when head MinTime >= maxt

units.headline: Test for the CompactSelectedSeries happy path
units.summary: New test checks that the selected series are evicted, the block carries the hint, HeadMinTime is unchanged, and the metrics are updated. It is test-only.

units.headline: Test that empty or nil refs are a no-op
units.summary: New test checks that nil and empty slices write no block and do not bump the triggered counter. It is test-only.

units.headline: Test that one hinted block is written per chunk range
units.summary: New test checks that a series spanning two chunk ranges produces two hinted blocks and is then evicted. It is test-only.
